You are building an admin product catalog page for an e-commerce team.

The catalog is read-heavy and should feel fast for day-to-day browsing, so avoid re-querying product data on every request.

Admins can trigger a "Sync latest catalog" action from the page when upstream ERP/PIM data changes (pricing, inventory, availability). After submitting, they should be able to continue working immediately, even if the product list is briefly stale.

The expected behavior is that product data is refreshed in the background and becomes up to date shortly after, across any views that depend on the same catalog data.

Implement the sync trigger as a regular HTML form that uses an inline Server Action in the page.
Use the cache tag name `"products"` consistently for catalog caching and invalidation.

In practice, sync jobs can touch thousands of SKUs, so operators prioritize a responsive admin experience and eventual consistency across catalog views over forcing every request to block on freshly recomputed data.
I'll start by inspecting the project and the Next.js caching docs so the catalog page can stay cached and refresh in the background after sync.

17 	The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.
18 	
19 	> **Good to know:**
20 	>
21 	> - To use cookies or headers, read them outside cached scopes and pass values as arguments. This is the preferred pattern.
22 	> - If the in-memory cache isn't sufficient for runtime data, [`'use cache: remote'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler, though it requires a network roundtrip to check the cache and typically incurs platform fees.
23 	> - For compliance requirements or when you can't refactor to pass runtime data as arguments to a `use cache` scope, see [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private).
24 	
25 	## Usage
26 	
27 	`use cache` is a Cache Components feature. To enable it, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your `next.config.ts` file:

30 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
31 	
32 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
33 	  cacheComponents: true,
34 	}
35 	
36 	export default nextConfig
37 	```
38 	
39 	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
40 	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
41 	const nextConfig = {
42 	  cacheComponents: true,
43 	}
44 	
45 	module.exports = nextConfig
46 	```
47 	
48 	Then, add `use cache` at the function, component, or file level. Cached functions and components must be async:
49 	
50 	```tsx

52 	export async function getData() {
53 	  'use cache'
54 	  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')

56 	  return data
57 	}
58 	
59 	// Component level
60 	export async function MyComponent() {
61 	  'use cache'
62 	  return <></>
63 	}
64 	```
65

67 	
68 	```tsx
69 	// File level
70 	'use cache'
71 	
72 	export default async function Page() {
73 	  // ...
74 	}
75 	```

8  	
9  	## Caching `fetch` requests
10 	
11 	By default, [`fetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) requests are not cached. You can cache individual requests by setting the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`.
12 	
13 	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
14 	export default async function Page() {
15 	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
16 	}
17 	```
18 	
19 	```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
20 	export default async function Page() {
21 	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
22 	}
23 	```
24 	
25 	See the [`fetch` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) to learn more.
26 	
27 	### `unstable_cache` for non-`fetch` functions
28 	
29 	`unstable_cache` allows you to cache the result of database queries and other async functions that don't use `fetch`. Wrap `unstable_cache` around the function:
30 	
31 	```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
32 	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
33 	import { db } from '@/lib/db'
34 	
35 	export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
36 	  async (id: string) => {
37 	    return db
38 	      .select()
39 	      .from(users)
40 	      .where(eq(users.id, id))
41 	      .then((res) => res[0])
42 	  },
43 	  ['user'], // cache key prefix
44 	  {
45 	    tags: ['user'],
46 	    revalidate: 3600,
47 	  }
48 	)
49 	```
50 	
51 	```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
52 	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
53 	import { db } from '@/lib/db'
54 	
55 	export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
56 	  async (id) => {
57 	    return db
58 	      .select()
59 	      .from(users)
60 	      .where(eq(users.id, id))
61 	      .then((res) => res[0])
62 	  },
63 	  ['user'], // cache key prefix
64 	  {
65 	    tags: ['user'],
66 	    revalidate: 3600,
67 	  }
68 	)
69 	```
70 	
71 	The third argument accepts:
72 	
73 	- `tags`: an array of tags for on-demand revalidation with `revalidateTag`.
74 	- `revalidate`: the number of seconds before the cache is revalidated.
75 	
76 	See the [`unstable_cache` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) to learn more.
77 	
78 	### Route segment config
79 	
80 	You can configure caching behavior at the route level by exporting config options from a [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
81 	
82 	#### `dynamic`
83 	
84 	Change the dynamic behavior of a layout or page to fully static or fully dynamic.
85 	
86 	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
87 	export const dynamic = 'auto'
88 	// 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
89 	```
90 	
91 	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
92 	export const dynamic = 'auto'
93 	// 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
94 	```
95 	
96 	- **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache as much as possible without preventing any components from opting into dynamic behavior.
97 	- **`'force-dynamic'`**: Force [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering), which will result in routes being rendered for each user at request time. This option is equivalent to:
98 	  - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'no-store', next: { revalidate: 0 } }`.

1  	---
2  	title: updateTag
3  	description: API Reference for the updateTag function.
4  	---
5  	
6  	`updateTag` allows you to update cached data on-demand for a specific cache tag from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data).
7  	
8  	This function is designed for **read-your-own-writes** scenarios, where a user makes a change (like creating a post), and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data.
9  	
10 	## Usage
11 	
12 	`updateTag` can **only** be called from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). It cannot be used in Route Handlers, Client Components, or any other context.
13 	
14 	If you need to invalidate cache tags in Route Handlers or other contexts, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) instead.
15 	
16 	> **Good to know**: `updateTag` immediately expires the cached data for the specified tag. The next request will wait to fetch fresh data rather than serving stale content from the cache, ensuring users see their changes immediately.
17 	
18 	## Parameters
19 	
20 	```tsx
21 	updateTag(tag: string): void;
22 	```
23 	
24 	- `tag`: A string representing the cache tag associated with the data you want to update. Must not exceed 256 characters. This value is case-sensitive.
25

19 	
20 	A **Server Action** is a [React Server Function](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) invoked through React's action mechanisms, such as `<form action>`, `<button formAction>`, or a client-side transition.
21 	
22 	You create one by adding the [`'use server'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-server) directive, then invoke it from a form, or from an event handler or `useEffect` wrapped in `startTransition`. For the basics of creating and invoking Server Functions, see [Mutating data](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) and the [Forms guide](/docs/app/guides/forms).
23 	
24 	This page covers the parts of Server Actions that are specific to Next.js: how they commonly map to mutations, how the response carries both returned data and re-rendered UI, how the client dispatches them, the security boundary the framework enforces, and the configuration available.
25 	
26 	## Sequential dispatch on the client
27 	
28 	Next.js dispatches Server Actions one at a time per client. If a user triggers three actions in quick succession, the second waits for the first to finish, then the third waits for the second. This keeps the re-rendered server tree consistent with the action result that produced it.
29

1 	---
2 	title: unstable_cache
3 	description: API Reference for the unstable_cache function.
4 	---
5 	
6 	> **Note:**
7 	> This API has been replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) in Next.js 16.
8 	> We recommend opting into [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and replacing `unstable_cache` with the `use cache` directive.
9 	
10	`unstable_cache` allows you to cache the results of expensive operations, like database queries, and reuse them across multiple requests.
11	
12	```jsx
13	import { getUser } from './data';
14	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache';
15	
16	const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
17	  async (id) => getUser(id),
18	  ['my-app-user']
19	);
20	
21	export default async function Component({ userID }) {
22	  const user = await getCachedUser(userID);
23	  ...
24	}
25	```
26	
27	> **Good to know**:
28	>
29	> - Accessing request data such as `headers` or `cookies` inside a cache scope is not supported. Read the data outside the cached function and pass the values you need as arguments.
30	> - This API uses Next.js' built-in cache to persist the result across requests and deployments. See [Caching and Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/caching).
31	
32	## Unsupported operations
33	
34	The function passed to `unstable_cache` cannot depend on the incoming request. Read values from `cookies()` or `headers()` before calling the cached function, then pass those values as arguments so they become part of the cache key.
35	
36	The cached function also cannot:
37	
38	- Call `connection()`, which requires an incoming request
39	- Enable or disable draft mode
40	- Call `revalidateTag()`, `updateTag()`, or `revalidatePath()` during cache execution
41	- Call a function that uses the `use cache: private` directive
42	
43	Perform request-dependent work before calling the cached function. Perform mutations and revalidation afterward from a Server Action or Route Handler.
44	
45	## Parameters
46	
47	```jsx
48	const data = unstable_cache(fetchData, keyParts, options)()
49	```
50	
51	- `fetchData`: This is an asynchronous function that fetches the data you want to cache. It must be a function that returns a `Promise`.
52	- `keyParts`: This is an extra array of keys that further adds identification to the cache. By default, `unstable_cache` already uses the arguments and the stringified version of your function as the cache key. It is optional in most cases; the only time you need to use it is when you use external variables without passing them as parameters. However, it is important to add closures used within the function if you do not pass them as parameters.
53	- `options`: This is an object that controls how the cache behaves. It can contain the following properties:
54	  - `tags`: An array of tags that can be used to control cache invalidation. Next.js will not use this to uniquely identify the function.
55	  - `revalidate`: The number of seconds after which the cache should be revalidated. Omit or pass `false` to cache indefinitely or until matching `revalidateTag()` or `revalidatePath()` methods are called.
56	
57	## Returns
58	
59	`unstable_cache` returns a function that when invoked, returns a Promise that resolves to the cached data. If the data is not in the cache, the provided function will be invoked, and its result will be cached and returned.
60	
61	## Example
62	
63	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher

events.content:
The admin catalog now reads from a shared `products` cache and syncs without blocking the page.

- Product reads go through `getAllProducts()` with `use cache`, `cacheTag('products')`, and `cacheLife('max')`, so browsing does not hit the database on every request.
- The "Sync latest catalog" control is a normal form whose inline Server Action calls `revalidateTag('products', 'max')`. That marks every catalog view stale and refreshes it in the background, so the admin can keep working while the list is briefly stale.
- `cacheComponents` is enabled so that tag can be invalidated on demand.

`npx next build` completed successfully. `/` prerendered as static with a 30-day revalidate and a 1-year expire.
